lines.text: Do you know how a zipper works? It's just two rows of teeth, and one clever little slider.
Each tooth has a bump on top and a hollow underneath. The rows are offset, so every tooth fits between two teeth on the other side.
The slider is a Y-shaped tunnel. Pull it up, and it squeezes the rows together at just the right angle, so each bump snaps into a hollow.
Pull it down, and a small wedge inside pushes the teeth apart again, one by one.
The modern zipper was patented in nineteen seventeen by Gideon Sundback. Before that, it was buttons and hooks.
So every zip is a row of tiny locks, closed by one small tunnel.
